briefing.text: Measure 'variance explained in PC1' by each categorical factor as R2 (eta-squared): regress the PC1 cell scores on the one-hot encoded factor (one-way ANOVA, PC1 ~ C(factor)), R2 = between-group SS / total SS of PC1, done separately for cytokine, donor, cell type and treatment. Do not use correlation with integer-coded labels or the PC's explained-variance ratio.
briefing.reason: The wrong metric produces a meaningless ranking; this defines the core computation.

briefing.text: The design is likely unbalanced (cell-type composition may differ by donor or cytokine), so marginal, sequential (Type-I) and adjusted (Type-II) R2 can rank factors differently. Crosstab cell_type x donor and cell_type x cytokine. Report marginal (one-factor-at-a-time) R2 as the primary answer; if Type-II gives a different order, flag it.
briefing.reason: Fixes which R2 variant to rank on, so a confounded design does not silently change the answer.

briefing.text: Plain R2 rises with the number of levels: a 91-level cytokine factor picks up some variance by chance, but a 2-level treatment factor cannot. Compare R2 with adjusted R2 and with a permutation null (shuffled labels) for each factor. With very many cells the inflation is usually small, so check it rather than assume it.
briefing.reason: Cytokine and donor/cell type may be close, and level-count inflation could flip their order.

briefing.text: Treatment (PBS vs cytokine) is probably a coarsening of the cytokine factor (PBS is one cytokine level), so R2(treatment) <= R2(cytokine) by construction. Confirm with a crosstab. Do not enter treatment after cytokine in a joint sequential model (it would get 0); use marginal R2 for each.
briefing.reason: Explains the structural relationship between two of the factors and prevents a modelling error.

briefing.text: Check whether X holds raw counts or log-normalized values. PC1 of unnormalized counts often tracks sequencing depth. Use the standard pipeline (normalize_total 1e4, log1p, ~2000 HVGs, scale max_value=10, PCA) before regressing PC1, then correlate PC1 with total counts / genes detected. If depth correlation stays high, report it and check whether depth differs by donor or cell type.
briefing.reason: Preprocessing decides what PC1 captures and so which factor it aligns with.

briefing.text: Check that the ranking holds by recomputing the PC1 factor R2 under at least two reasonable settings (e.g. HVG+scaling vs no scaling, or a different subsample seed). If the top factor changes, report the standard scanpy pipeline as primary and note the instability.
briefing.reason: A ranking that only holds under one pipeline is not trustworthy.

briefing.text: The h5ad is large (~1.6 GB). If you subsample, stratify (e.g. equal cells per sample or per cytokine x donor) and compare factor level counts before and after. Otherwise use backed mode or full data with sparse/arpack PCA. Naive random subsampling can distort the design and bias per-factor R2.
briefing.reason: Practical memory constraint whose naive workaround can bias the result.

briefing.text: Sanity-check the R2 ranking against PC1's top-loading genes. Lineage markers (CD3E, CD14, MS4A1, NKG7) point to cell type, interferon/cytokine-response genes point to cytokine, and sex/HLA genes (XIST, RPS4Y1, HLA) point to donor. If the loadings disagree with the R2 ranking, recheck the preprocessing.
briefing.reason: Gives an independent biological check on the computed ranking.

shared_assumptions: Both teams treat each of ~100k cells as an independent observation and compute cell-level one-way eta^2; cells are clustered within 1092 donor x cytokine samples, so 'variance explained' could instead be read at the sample (pseudobulk) level.
Both teams used one pipeline family (total-count 1e4, log1p, 2000 HVG, scale, PCA on all cells); HVGs were not chosen per donor/batch and no QC filter (mito %, gene_count) was applied before PCA.
Both teams take the obs 'cell_type' (18 fine labels) as the cell-type factor as given; a coarser grouping (lineage) or the fine labels could change only cell-type R2, which is far ahead either way.
Both teams assume PBS counts as one of the '91 cytokines', so treatment is nested in cytokine and cytokine R2 >= treatment R2 by construction.
unused_evidence: obs 'sample' (1092 levels = donor x cytokine) was not used, e.g. to aggregate or to test sample-level variation on PC1.

Split-pool barcode wells bc1_well/bc2_well/bc3_well (and bc*_wind) are technical plate/well identifiers; neither team checked whether PC1 carries a well/plate effect that is aliased with donor or cytokine.

QC columns pct_counts_MT, total_counts_MT, gene_count, tscp_count, mread_count were used only for one depth correlation (team A); neither team checked whether a low-quality/high-MT subpopulation drives part of PC1 or the donor term.
var 'n_cells' was not used to filter rarely detected genes before HVG selection.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: cytokine vs treatment order rests on R2 values near the permutation null; reported, partially resolved via adjusted R2, but the ordering is also guaranteed by nesting, so it is not an independent confirmation.

Team B: donor eta^2 may reflect donor cell-type composition; team B only reported this. Team A showed donor Type-II R2 (0.002) still exceeds cytokine (0.0006), which resolves the ordering under that model, but neither team checked donor vs cytokine at the pseudobulk level.
second_readings: 'Variance explained in PC1' could mean PCA on pseudobulk profiles (per sample, or per sample x cell type) rather than on single cells; at sample level the cell-type factor can disappear or change scale, and donor vs cytokine could reorder.
'Cytokine identity (which of 91 cytokines)' could be read as excluding PBS (cytokine-treated cells only); team B checked this and found the ranking unchanged.
challenge.verdict: High trust in A: the gaps are large (cell type ~0.96, donor ~0.10, cytokine ~0.002, treatment ~0.0002), cytokine >= treatment holds by nesting, and team A's Type-II check keeps donor above cytokine. The remaining risk is a pseudobulk reading of the task, which might reorder donor vs cytokine. Neither team has tested it.

Which tools (e.g. scater getVarianceExplained, variancePartition) do which by default?
questions.why: Settles whether the cell-level eta^2 both teams used is the conventional quantity, or whether a sample-level reading could rank donor and the perturbation factor differently.

questions.why: Shows whether the unused barcode-well columns can confound the donor or perturbation terms on PC1.

findings.question: When single-cell studies report the 'variance explained' in a principal component by categorical metadata (e.g. donor, cell type, perturbation), is this usually computed as R2 from a linear model of cell-level PC scores, or on pseudobulk profiles? Which tools (e.g. scater getVarianceExplained, variancePartition) do which by default?
findings.answer: Cell-level is the convention for PC-variance-explained. scater getExplanatoryPCs (which calls getVarianceExplained) regresses each PC on each colData variable separately over all columns (cells, in an SCE) and reports percent R2, i.e. marginal one-way R2 (eta^2 for a factor). variancePartition fits a linear mixed model on whatever columns it is given; it was designed for bulk samples, and its single-cell use goes through dreamlet, which first aggregates to pseudobulk (sample x cell type) and analyses each cell type separately. In that setup cell type is not a factor within an assay, so a pseudobulk reading cannot rank cell type against donor in the same way. The cell-level eta^2 the teams used is the standard quantity for this question.
findings.text: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: When single-cell studies report the 'variance explained' in a principal component by categorical metadata (e.g. donor, cell type, perturbation), is this usually computed as R2 from a linear model of cell-level PC scores, or on pseudobulk profiles? Which tools (e.g. scater getVarianceExplained, variancePartition) do which by default? ANSWER: Cell-level is the convention for PC-variance-explained. scater getExplanatoryPCs (which calls getVarianceExplained) regresses each PC on each colData variable separately over all columns (cells, in an SCE) and reports percent R2, i.e. marginal one-way R2 (eta^2 for a factor). variancePartition fits a linear mixed model on whatever columns it is given; it was designed for bulk samples, and its single-cell use goes through dreamlet, which first aggregates to pseudobulk (sample x cell type) and analyses each cell type separately. In that setup cell type is not a factor within an assay, so a pseudobulk reading cannot rank cell type against donor in the same way. The cell-level eta^2 the teams used is the standard quantity for this question. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: https://rdrr.io/bioc/scater/man/getVarianceExplained.html, https://rdrr.io/bioc/scater/man/getExplanatoryPCs.html, https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/variancePartition/inst/doc/variancePartition.html, https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/dreamlet/inst/doc/dreamlet.html.

findings.question: In split-pool combinatorial barcoding single-cell protocols, what does the first-round barcode well encode (sample identity or something else), and is it a recognized source of technical batch effects?
findings.answer: The round-1 well barcode is added by in-cell reverse transcription and is the sample-specific barcode (Parse: 'the first sample-specific barcodes are added by in-cell reverse transcription'), so it encodes sample/condition identity. In Parse/SPLiT-seq v2 each well also holds paired oligo-dT and random-hexamer barcodes, which are collapsed to the same cell. Because the well is nested within sample (donor x condition), it is confounded with donor and perturbation by design and cannot be separated from them as an independent covariate. The pages I read mention sample-quality bias in split barcoding, but none of them describes round-1 wells as a recognized independent technical batch effect. The web did not settle the batch-effect part.
findings.confidence: high on what the well encodes; low on batch effects
